subject: Private patch cadence proposal and emergency rollback plan
messages:
From: Tim Hargreaves <tim.hargreaves@omnibank.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops-eng@omnibank.com
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: quarterly private patch cadence + emergency rollback expectations

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for taking a look. We run Redwood Private for a number of regulated workloads and we need an agreed-on cadence for non-disruptive security patches and a clear emergency rollback SLA. High-level asks from OmniBank: 

- Quarterly maintenance windows, but we can accept a narrow weekend window (Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC) — any longer windows must be pre-approved.
- Version pinning rules: we want control over major.minor (e.g., 1.5.x) and an ability to opt out of automatic minor rollups.
- Clear rollback criteria and expected RTO/RPO for production releases.
- Preflight checklist and a short list of telemetry/thresholds you monitor so our SRE can validate the rollback decision.

Can you send a proposed cadence and the runbook (high-level) + an example of rollback triggers? We also need to know whether KV cache eviction and connection draining are part of your standard flow or a manual step.

Attachments: none (please attach your runbook).

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Hargreaves
Head of Cloud Ops — OmniBank

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tim Hargreaves <tim.hargreaves@omnibank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: quarterly private patch cadence + emergency rollback expectations

Tim — thanks for the clear asks. Sharing a concise proposal below and attaching the first draft runbook (patch-runbook-v1.pdf) and canary matrix.

Proposal (summary)
- Cadence: quarterly security/stability patch windows by default. Customers may opt into monthly security-only transients if they sign an opt-in schedule.
- Maintenance window: default weekend window (Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC). For narrow-window customers we offer a 02:00–04:00 UTC fast pass — this requires a 72-hour preflight and a tighter canary (5% traffic for 24h).
- Version pinning: we pin at two dimensions — model-serving artifact (git tag) and runtime image. Pin format we propose: major.minor+build (example: 1.5+build-20251010). Minor revs are non-breaking patches; customers can request "minor freeze" to opt out for a quarter.
- Rollback triggers (automatic/manual):
  * Automatic fallback: sustained error rate >= 3x baseline for 5 minutes or p95 latency regression > 200 ms for 10 minutes.
  * Manual rollback: any validated data corruption, leak causing OOMs, or sustained availability < 99.5% after 15 minutes.
- Rollback RTO objective: 30 minutes to failover to previous pinned variant for single-region impact. RPO: best-effort for in-flight requests; we recommend app-level idempotency for critical writes.

Operational steps (high level)
1) Preflight: smoke tests, KV cache snapshot, model artifact checksum verification, canary slice staging. (See attached patch-runbook-v1.pdf)
2) Drain policy: connection drain + 5s grace for existing requests; then target-level traffic shift to canary.
3) KV cache: we take a hot-snapshot before rolling and keep it for 48h; eviction is automatic for prefix caches but we offer a manual flush if requested.
4) Network quiesce: BGP/route changes are not expected; we use local node cordon + traffic shift.

Canary plan: 5% for 2 hours, then 25% for 4 hours, then full ramp if stable (see canary-matrix.xlsx).

Next steps: 1) Confirm the weekend window above for OmniBank, 2) confirm whether you want the 02:00–04:00 fast pass, 3) sign-off on rollback triggers + attachments. I can schedule a 45-minute preflight run now that the runbook is attached.

Attachments:
- patch-runbook-v1.pdf (high-level checklist + telemetry thresholds)
- canary-matrix.xlsx (detailed traffic ramp)
- maintenance-calendar.ics (proposal dates)

Thanks,
- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.com <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, Tim Hargreaves <tim.hargreaves@omnibank.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: quarterly private patch cadence + emergency rollback expectations

On Tue, Nov 4, 2025 at 8:12 AM karthik_iyer@redwood.com wrote:
> Proposal (summary)
> - Cadence: quarterly security/stability patch windows by default...

Quick technical notes / addenda from infra: 
- Pinning: we need to be explicit in the runbook about pin metadata that gets stored in the control plane: {image_tag, model_hash, kv_snapshot_id, rollout_id}. That metadata is essential for deterministic rollback.
- Cache snapshot: we do a lightweight prefix checkpoint (TTL-preserving) and store a snapshot id; full rebuild path exists but is slow. Recommend keeping snapshot retention to 72h for high-compliance customers.
- KV eviction: automatic eviction works for prefixed app caches; however session-affinity caches must be drained manually — callout in the runbook.
- Network maintenance: for on-prem customers who manage their own network, we include a two-step guidance: (1) cordon + local drain, (2) announce health-check bypass route for open connections — sample commands included in runbook v1.
- Canary gating: add a synthetic-traffic probe set (30 qps of representative traffic) in addition to real traffic; this detects hidden regressions in ordering/serialization.

I suggest we set the fast-pass window only for customers that complete the 72h preflight. Also, for rollback criteria, add a manual confirm step via CS/Eng before a full rollback (we can automate partial rollback).

I attached a short diff to the runbook in the drive link (see related_links).

— Irene
Irene Choi
Lead SRE, Private Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Tim Hargreaves <tim.hargreaves@omnibank.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: quarterly private patch cadence + emergency rollback expectations

Thanks — this is a good, practical proposal.

Action items I approve: 
- Adopt the quarterly cadence with an opt-in monthly security-only flow.
- Default weekend window (Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC), with a 02:00–04:00 fast pass for customers that finish the 72h preflight.
- The rollback triggers and RTO objective look reasonable; add the manual CS confirm before full failback.

Karthik: please update the runbook with Irene's metadata block and the synthetic-probe step.
Irene: please add the snapshot retention note and the manual session-affinity flush steps.
Neha: coordinate with Sales/CS to finalize the customer opt-in language and sign-off flow.

I'll schedule the preflight sync for Nov 12, 2025 16:00 UTC (45 minutes). Tim — can you confirm that slot works for OmniBank? If yes, I'll send the calendar invite and the preflight agenda.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
